steps.body:
This practice has three moves.

First, you describe someone through a strong reaction — 'he is,' 'she does.' Then you speak directly to them. Then you write as them.

The quality that charges you most in others often lives in you — in a different form, unexpressed, unrecognized.

steps.title: Someone is pulling your attention.
steps.body: Through irritation, envy, admiration, contempt — whoever has charge right now. Describe them in third person. What are they like? What do they do?
steps.placeholder: Describe them as you'd describe them to someone else…

steps.title: How strong is the pull?
steps.body: Dark or bright — the strength is the signal.

steps.title: Now speak directly to them.
steps.body: Write as 'you.' 'You are ___. When you ___, I feel ___.' Let it be unfiltered — they're not here.

steps.title: Now become them.
steps.body: Write as them. 'I am ___. I carry ___. What I want you to know is ___.' You're not pretending — you're exploring what of yours they might be carrying.

steps.title: Having moved through all three — what quality did you recognize in yourself?
steps.body: Name it, even if you're not sure.

exit.body: You moved from observing, to relating, to recognizing. That's the full circuit.
